title: ComponentValidator
description: A single declarative custom validator attached to a component. Failing entries with severity 'error' contribute to FormGroup.invalid through the existing form.valid gate, blocking NEXT/SAVE. For aggregating components without a real FormControl (DataTable, DocumentGrid, ...), the framework registers a shadow FormControl named '<componentName>__validity' on the parent FormGroup that carries this validator's errors.

allOf.comment: 3-way XOR: at most ONE of dataFetcher / dataFetchers / fetcher (Phase 2). Zero is fine — that's a client-only validator (Phase 1).

key.description: Stable identifier for this validator. Surfaces as FormControl.errors[key]. Must be unique within a single component's validators array.

expression.description: JavaScript expression evaluated in context { value, source, form } plus global tokens (${...}). Truthy = valid; falsy/string = invalid (a returned string overrides 'message'). Inside row expressions, r.Field is the RAW backend value (not token-substituted) — SQL bit/boolean columns often serialize as the string 'true'/'false', so prefer a type-robust comparison (=== true || === 'true') over a strict === true. Note [].every() returns true (an empty table passes); guard with value.items.length > 0 if that's not intended.

message.description: Error text rendered when the expression returns falsy. Supports ${...} token interpolation against the same context as expression. Missing tokens render as empty strings; the validator still applies.
examples: All application forms must be signed before continuing.

when.description: Optional gate expression. When falsy, the validator is skipped (treated as valid). Same DSL as 'expression'.

validateOn.description: When the validator runs. Defaults to 'onChange' (reactive). Use 'onSave' to defer expensive backend probes to save time; the submit flow awaits any pending probe through the save-time barrier. For explicit-only firing (polling, 'Re-check' buttons) compose onChange with a sibling DataFetcher's manualTrigger flag and the 'revalidate' event verb — no separate trigger value is needed.

severity.description: Severity of the failure. Only 'error' blocks form.valid; 'warning' and 'info' are advisory-only. Accepts a literal value OR a ${...} token expression that resolves to one at evaluation time (e.g. "${result.data.severity}"). Invalid resolution falls back to 'error' with a console warning.

dataFetcher.description: Phase 2 — inline single-fetcher sugar. The probe result is exposed to 'expression' / 'message' as the local 'result'. Mutually exclusive with 'dataFetchers' and 'fetcher'.

dataFetchers.description: Phase 2 — inline multi-fetcher map. Each key surfaces its envelope to 'expression' / 'message' (e.g. key 'dup' is referenced as dup.ok, dup.data, dup.error). Reserved keys: 'value', 'source', 'form', 'result'. Mutually exclusive with 'dataFetcher' and 'fetcher'.

propertyNames.description: Map keys become identifiers in the expression sandbox, so they must be valid JS identifiers and may not collide with the reserved sandbox locals 'value', 'source', 'form', 'result'.

fetcher.description: Phase 2 escape hatch — name of a sibling <dataFetcher> component on the same form. Use when the validator needs the full DataFetcher surface. Mutually exclusive with 'dataFetcher' and 'dataFetchers'.

inlineDataFetcher.description: Narrow projection of DataFetcher carrying only the fields a validator needs to probe a backend dataSource. No name, manualTrigger, or events — those belong to a full <dataFetcher> component referenced via 'fetcher'.

dataSourcePath.description: Relative path to the backend dataSource. Required.

parameters.description: Parameter bindings sent with the probe. Supports the same token DSL as DataFetcher parameters plus the validator-local '${value}' sandbox identifier.

valueExpression.description: Optional post-processing expression evaluated against the raw response. When present, validator expressions see the result as 'data' instead of the raw payload.

timeoutMs.description: Per-fetcher timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to engine default (10000ms). On timeout, envelope resolves with error.code 'TIMEOUT' and the validator fails closed.
